answerText:
No. The filing representative cannot attest for the applicant or owner, or submit this job filing. The applicant must electronically sign the filing, including a final electronic signature at preview, and officially submits the job filing. The owner must complete the Owner’s Attestation to authorize the applicant and acknowledge review of the application; all job filings require that confirmation. [DOB NOW application user guide, p. 38](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_application_user_guide.pdf#page=38) [Filing through DOB NOW: Build — attestation, preview and submission](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/filing-through-dob-now-build.page)

A filing representative may enter and view filing information and make payments on associated jobs, but cannot submit filings or permits. Thus, completed data entry and uploaded documents do not substitute for the applicant’s and owner’s required attestations or permit representative submission. [DOB NOW: Build FAQs — Owner and Professional Responsibilities](https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/industry/dob-now-build-faqs.page)

If the Owner Type is Condo Unit Owner or Co-Op Tenant-Shareholder, the Board representative is also a required stakeholder and both the owner and Board representative must attest before the filing can proceed. [DOB NOW: Build release notes, p. 20](https://www.nyc.gov/assets/buildings/pdf/dob_now_build_release_notes.pdf#page=20)

Official supporting guidance — noncontrolling and not an enacted-code conclusion.
